title: Fed decision, October 2026 meeting
note: Kalshi's 0 bps bucket and Polymarket's 'no change' market both price the Fed holding rates at the October 2026 meeting.
kalshi_rule: Yes if the Fed hikes by 0 bps at the October 28, 2026 meeting, per the FOMC statement.
polymarket_rule: Yes if the upper bound of the target fed funds range is unchanged after the October 27-28, 2026 FOMC meeting.
rules_note: Both resolve from the same FOMC statement, so Kalshi's 0 bps bucket and Polymarket's 'no change' bracket settle together.

title: US CPI, month-over-month, September 2026
note: CPI is published to one decimal, so Kalshi's 'more than 0.7%' is Polymarket's '0.8% or more'. Both settle on the BLS September 2026 CPI release.
kalshi_rule: Yes if BLS reports September 2026 CPI up more than 0.7% month-over-month, quoted to one decimal.
polymarket_rule: Yes if the seasonally adjusted CPI-U one-month change for September 2026 is 0.8% or more, at one-decimal precision.
rules_note: Same BLS report and the same one-decimal scale, on which 'more than 0.7%' and '0.8% or more' cut at the same place; they differ on which series has to clear it - Polymarket names the seasonally adjusted CPI-U, while Kalshi's rule says only 'the Consumer Price Index' and leaves the adjustment unstated.

title: US nonfarm payrolls, October 2026
note: Both settle on the BLS Employment Situation report for October 2026; Kalshi says 'above 100000' where Polymarket says 'at least 100k'.
kalshi_rule: Yes if the BLS October 2026 Employment Situation reports nonfarm payroll growth above 100,000.
polymarket_rule: Yes if the BLS October 2026 report shows at least 100,000 jobs added, with values falling between brackets resolving to the higher one.
rules_note: Same BLS release, but the threshold differs at exactly 100,000: Kalshi needs growth strictly above it, while Polymarket accepts it and sends values between brackets to the higher one.
